title: B14
note: The ONLY hand-written part of build 14's reference manifest. Everything else is derived from the source's input.* defaults. Each entry says why it is not at its default; an override without a reason is indistinguishable from the drift this mechanism exists to catch.

in_22.why: DVB order-flow display scope. Deliberate, as found; not a decision input.

in_23.why: DVB bubble volume percentile. Deliberate, as found.

in_29.why: DVB filter type. Deliberate, as found.

in_42.why: SESX entry session, exchange timezone. As found. FLAGGED: the recorded champion for this lever is 2000-1400, so this is an open discrepancy - left unchanged here deliberately, because changing it in the same run as the three lever corrections would confound the two.

in_46.why: The study's own timeframe. Must match the chart resolution or every figure describes a different series.

in_94.why: Active order-block selection rule. Decision-relevant; deliberate, as found.

in_250.why: Census log.info lines off. Logging only - and on at 45S it floods the Pine log.

in_278.why: PYRX - add on same-direction CZ breaks. Found ON against a default of false. Off is the source default and the recorded intent. With it on, TradingView pairs stacked exits FIFO, so per-row attribution inside a stack is TradingView's construct - which is exactly what a top-three-winners statistic measures.

in_315.why: RVX - take the opposite side after a CZX hard stop. Found ON against a default of false. REFUTED on deep+OOS, n=117: +0.147/trade, PF 1.06, t=0.29.

in_323.why: OPPX - re-enter on the opposite CZ break. Found ON against a default of false. REFUTED on deep: -45.88 (496.76 to 450.88), PF 1.92 to 1.62.

properties._why: in_328..in_352 are TradingView's STRATEGY PROPERTIES, not Pine source. They cannot be derived from the script and they decide what a backtest means - costs, fills, stacking and the reported statistics - so they are pinned by hand. Verified against the chart, not copied from it: each value below is the TradingView default except in_344, which is called out.

in_328.why: Initial capital. The denominator of every percentage figure.

in_330.why: Order size - 1 contract, which is why every trade row carries q=1 and per-leg MAE is unambiguous.

in_332.why: 0.11 per side, 0.22 round trip. This is the constant inside every MAE and MFE figure.

in_333.why: Slippage. Zero, so every net figure is optimistic by the real spread.

in_336.why: TradingView-level pyramiding allowance. Inert once PYRX is off, because the script stops requesting stacked entries.

in_338.why: Do not process orders on bar close - orders fill intrabar.

in_339.why: Do not recalculate after an order fills.

in_341.why: Base currency - report stays in the account currency, USD.

in_342.why: Exit pairing rule. Load-bearing while a position can hold more than one leg; moot once PYRX is off.

in_343.why: Risk free rate, 2%. FLAGGED: this setting exists and an earlier note said no risk-free-rate setting was exposed. Whether TradingView applies it to the displayed Sharpe is a separate question and is tested, not assumed.

in_344.why: Bar Magnifier ON - the one property away from its default. It changes intrabar fill simulation in Deep Backtesting, so it is held fixed across every window and every A/B configuration; changing it would move the fills under the comparison.

in_345.why: Do not fill orders using standard OHLC.

in_347.why: Alert message template - unused in backtest mode.

in_348.why: Alert type. The alert surface is order fills only, which is the ALRTX finding.

in_352.why: Do not calculate on every history tick.
